slot.brief: Simple sentence divided into parts, one containing a basic tense error (e.g., present perfect with a past-time adverb like 'yesterday'); ask which part has the error.

stem:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
(A) The clerk
(B) has stamped the parcel
(C) yesterday
(D) before the post office closed.

verdicts.working: “Yesterday” specifies a completed past time, so the verb should be simple past: “stamped,” not “has stamped.”

working:
“Yesterday” specifies a finished past time, so the present perfect “has stamped” is incorrect; use “stamped.” The remaining parts are grammatically sound.
